questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=xe^{-x}\). The maximum value of the function in the interval \((0,\infty )\) is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} f(x)&=xe^{-x}\\ f'(x)&=e^{-x}-xe^{-x}=0\\ e^{-x}(1-x)&=0\\ x&=1\\ f''(x)&=-e^{-x}-e^{-x}+xe^{-x}\\ &=e^{-x}(x-2)\\ f''(1)&=e^{-1}(-1)=-e^{-1} \lt 0 \end{aligned}\]
Hence f(x) has maximum value at x=1
\(f(1)=1\cdot e^{-1}=e^{-1}\)

questions.question:
The solution for the differential equation
\(\frac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}}=-9x\)
with initial conditions x(0)=1 and \(\frac{dx}{dt}|_{t=0}=1\), is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} \frac{d^2x}{dt^2}&=-9x\\ \frac{d^2x}{dt^2}+9x&=0\\ (D^2+9)x &=0 \end{aligned}\]
Auxiliary equation is \(m^2+9=0\)
\[\begin{aligned} m&= \pm 3i\\ x&= C_1 \cos 3t+C_2 \sin 3t\;\;...(i)\\ x(0) &=1\;\;i.e.\;x\rightarrow 1\; when t\rightarrow 0 \\ 1&=C_1 \\ \frac{dx}{dt}&=-3C_1 \sin 3t+3C_2 \cos 3t\;\;...(ii) \\ x'(0)&=1\;\; i.e.\;x'\rightarrow 1\; when \; t\rightarrow 0 \\ 1&=3C_2 \\ C_2&=\frac{1}{3}\\ \therefore \;x&=\cos 3t+\frac{1}{3}\sin 3t \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: electromagnetic-fields
questions.question: \(C_0\) is the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air as dielectric (as in figure (a)). If, half of the entire gap as shown in figure (b) is filled with a dielectric of permittivity \(\epsilon _r\) , the expression for the modified capacitance is
questions.explanation:
Let A be the area of the parallel plate capacitor and d be the distance between the plates.

Let \(C_1\) be the capacitance of half portion with air as dielectic medium and \(C_2\) be capacitance with a dielectic of permitivity, \(\varepsilon _r\).
Then, \(C_1=\frac{\varepsilon _0 \left ( \frac{A}{2} \right )}{d}\) (As area become half)
and \(C_2=\frac{\varepsilon _0 \varepsilon _r \left ( \frac{A}{2} \right )}{d}\) (As area becomes half)
Now, these two capacitance will be in parallel if a voltage is applied between the plates as same potential difference will be there between both the capacitance.

Equivalent capacitance is
\[\begin{aligned} C_{eqv} &= C_1+C_2\\ &=\frac{\varepsilon _0 A}{2d}+ \frac{\varepsilon _0 \varepsilon _r A}{2d}\\ &= \frac{\varepsilon _0 A}{2d}(1+ \varepsilon _r)=\frac{C_0}{2}(1+\varepsilon _r) \end{aligned}\]
Therefore, modified capacitance,
\(C_{eqv}=\frac{C_0}{2}(1+\varepsilon _r)\)

Given \(C=1\mu F, V_c(0)=-2V\), \(R=100\Omega , I=20mA\). Circuit fot the given condition at time \(t \gt 0\) is shown below:

Applying KVL, we have,\(V_s(s)=\left ( \frac{-2}{s} \right )+\frac{I}{s} \left ( R+\frac{I}{Cs} \right )\)
\(\;\;=\frac{1}{s}\left [ -2+IR+\frac{I}{Cs} \right ]\)
\(\;\;=\frac{1}{s}\left [ (IR-2) +\frac{I}{Cs}\right ]\)
Putting values of R, C and I, we get,
\(V_s(s)=\frac{1}{s}\left [ (20 \times 10^{-3} \times 200-2)+\left ( \frac{20 \times 10^{-3}}{10^{-6}} \right ) \times \frac{1}{s} \right ]\)
\(\;\;=\frac{1}{s}\left [ (2-2)+20 \times 10^3 \times \frac{1}{s} \right ]\)
\(\;\;=\frac{20 \times 10^3}{s^2}\)
\(\therefore \;\; V_s(s)=\frac{20 \times 10^3}{s^2}\)
\(V_s(t)=20000 t u(t)\)
\(\therefore \;\; V_s(s)=(20000)tu(t)\)
Which is equation of a straight line passing through origin. Hence option (C) is correct.

\(N_s=\frac{120f}{P}=\frac{120 \times 50}{8}=750 \text{rpm}\)
\[\begin{aligned} \therefore \;\;\text{Slip,}\;S&=\left ( \frac{N_s-N_r}{N_s} \right )\\ &= \left ( \frac{750-700}{750} \right )\\ &=\frac{50}{750}=\frac{1}{15} \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question:
A star connected 400 V, 50 Hz, 4 pole synchronous machine gave the following open circuit and short circuit test results :
Open circuit test : \(V_{oc}\) = 400 V (rms, line-to-line) at field current, \(I_{f}\) = 2.3 A
Short circuit test : \(I_{sc}\)= 10 A (rms, phase) at field current, \(I_{f}\) = 1.5 A

The value of per phase synchronous impedance in \(\Omega\) at rated voltage is_____.
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} \text{Given, for}\;\;V_{OC} &= 400V(rms)\\ &= \frac{400}{\sqrt{3}}\\ &= 230.94 \;\text{(Phase value),}\\ I_f&= 2.3A\\ \text{for}\;\; I_{sc}&=10A \;\text{(rms, phase)} \\ I_f&= 1.5A\\ & \therefore \;\;\text{Base impedance}\\ Z_{base}&=\frac{V_{OC}}{I_{sc}}\\ &=\frac{230.94}{10}=23.094\Omega \end{aligned}\]
For finding the synchronous impedance at rated voltage, saturation effect of the machine has to be considered (i.e. the adjusted value of \(Z_s\))
short circuit ratio,
\[\begin{aligned} SCR &=\frac{I_f \;for \; V_{OC}}{I_f \;for \; I_{sc}} \\ &=\frac{1}{Z_{s_{(sat)pu}}} =\frac{2.3}{1.5}\\ Z_{s_{(sat)pu}} &= 0.65 pu \end{aligned}\]
Therefore, actual value of \(Z_s\) at rated voltage
\[\begin{aligned} &=Z_{s_{(sat)pu}} \times Z_{base} \\ &=0.65 \times 23.094=15.06\Omega \\ \therefore \;\;Z_s&= 15.06\Omega \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: The line integral of function F=yzi, in the counterclockwise direction, along the circle \(x^{2}+y^{2}=1\) at z=1 is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} \bar{F} &=yz\hat{i} \\ \bigtriangledown \times \bar{F} &=\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ \frac{\partial }{\partial x} & \frac{\partial }{\partial y} &\frac{\partial }{\partial z} \\ yz& 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix} \\ &= \hat{i}(0)-\hat{j}(0-y)+\hat{k}(0-z)\\ &=0\hat{i}+y\hat{j}-z\hat{k} \end{aligned}\]
By strokes theoram,
\[\begin{aligned} \int _C\bar{F}\cdot d\bar{r}&=\int _S (\bigtriangledown \times \bar{F})\cdot \hat{n}ds\\ &=\int _S (y\hat{j}-z\hat{k})\cdot \hat{k}ds\\ &=\int _S -z \; ds \;\;\;\text{ Since }\; z=1\\ &=\int _S -1 \; ds=(-1)S=(-1)\pi =-\pi \end{aligned}\]
where S is surface area of \(x^2+y^2=1\)
\(\therefore \;\;S=\pi(1)^2=\pi\)

questions.question: An incandescent lamp is marked 40 W, 240 V. If resistance at room temperature (26\(^{\circ}\)C) is 120 \(\Omega\), and temperature coefficient of resistance is \(4.5\times 10^{-3}/^{\circ}\)C, then its 'ON' state filament temperature in \(^{\circ}\)C is approximately_____.
questions.explanation:
Let the resistance of incandescent lamp
\(=R_T=\frac{V^2}{P}=\frac{(240)^2}{40}=1440\Omega\)
Given, \(R_0=120\Omega ,\)
\(\alpha =4.5 \times 10^{-3}/^{\circ}C\)
Let, \(R_T\) be the resistance of the filament in ON state at temperature T.
Then, \(R_T=R_0[1+\alpha \Delta T]\)
\([1+\alpha \Delta T]=\frac{R_T}{R_0}=\frac{1440}{120}=12\)
\(\alpha \Delta T=11\)
\(\Delta T=2444.44^{\circ}C\)
\(T=2444.44^{\circ}C+26^{\circ}\)
\(T=2470.44^{\circ}C\)
Therefore, ON state temperature of filament \(= 2470.44^{\circ}C\)

questions.subject: power-systems
questions.question: In an unbalanced three phase system, phase current \(I_a = 1\angle -90^{\circ}\) pu, negative sequence current \(I_{b2}=4 \angle( -150^{\circ})\), zero sequence current \(I_{c0}=3 \angle -90^{\circ}\) pu. The magnitude of phase current \(I_{b}\)  in pu is
questions.explanation:
Given,
\[\begin{aligned} I_a&= 1\angle (-90^{\circ})pu\\ I_b&= 4\angle (-150^{\circ})pu\\ I_c&= 3\angle (90^{\circ})pu \end{aligned}\]
As zero sequence current in all the three phases of unbalanced \(3-\phi\) system are equal, therefore,
\(I_{a_0}=I_{b_0}=I_{c_0}=3\angle 90^{\circ}pu\)

Also, \(I_{b_2}=4\angle -150^{\circ}\)
=Negative phase sequence current of phase b.
Therefore, referring to the negative phase sequence phasor,
\(I_{b_2}=4\angle (-150^{\circ}-120^{\circ})=4\angle-270^{\circ}pu\)
We know that, phase current vectors in matrix form are given by
\[\begin{aligned} \begin{bmatrix} I_a\\ I_b\\ I_c \end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &1 &1 \\ 1& a^2 &a \\ 1 & a &a^2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} I_{a_0}\\ I_{a_1}\\ I_{a_2} \end{bmatrix} \\ \text{Here, } I_a&=I_{a_0}+I_{a_1}+I_{a_2} \\ \text{Given, } I_a&=1\angle -90^{\circ} \\ I_{a_0}&=3\angle 90^{\circ} \\ I_{a_2}&=4\angle -270^{\circ} \\ \text{Therefore,}& \\ I_{a_1}&=I_a-(I_{a_0}+I_{a_2}) \\ &=(1\angle -90^{\circ})-(3\angle 90^{\circ}+4\angle 270^{\circ}) \\ I_{a_1}&=8\angle -90^{\circ}pu \\ \text{Therefore,}& \\ I_b&=I_{a_0}+a^2I_{a_1}+aI_{a_2}\\ &=(3\angle 90^{\circ})+(1\angle 120^{\circ})^2 (8\angle -90^{\circ}) \\ &+(1\angle 120^{\circ})(4\angle -270^{\circ})\\ &=3\angle 90^{\circ}+8\angle 150^{\circ}+4\angle -150^{\circ}\\ I_b&=11.53\angle 154.3^{\circ}pu\\ &\text{Magnitude of phase current,}\\ I_b&=11.53\;pu \end{aligned}\]

\[\begin{aligned} f(t)&\rightleftharpoons F(\omega )\\ g(t)&=\int_{-\infty }^{\infty }F(u)e^{-jut}du\\ \text{Now, }f(t)&=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty }^{\infty }F(\omega)e^{j \omega t}d\omega \\ \Rightarrow \; 2 \pi f(t)&=\int_{-\infty }^{\infty }F(\omega)e^{j \omega t}d\omega \\ \omega &\rightarrow u,\\ 2 \pi f(t)&=\int_{-\infty }^{\infty }F(u)e^{j u t}du \\ t &\rightarrow -t,\\ 2 \pi f(-t)&=\int_{-\infty }^{\infty }F(u)e^{-j u t}du \\ &=g(t)\\ \Rightarrow \; g(t)&=2 \pi f(-t)\\ &= 2\pi f(t) \end{aligned}\]
[If \(f(t)\) is even then \(f(t)=f(-t)\)
\(\Rightarrow \;\; g(t) \propto f(t) \text{ if }f(t) \text{ is even.}\)

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question: The core loss of a single phase, 230/115 V, 50 Hz power transformer is measured from 230 V side by feeding the primary (230 V side) from a variable voltage variable frequency source while keeping the secondary open circuited. The core loss is measured to be 1050 W for 230 V, 50 Hz input. The core loss is again measured to be 500 W for 138 V, 30 Hz input. The hysteresis and eddy current losses of the transformer for 230 V, 50 Hz input are respectively,
questions.explanation:
Given, at 230V, 50 Hz, core loss =1050 W
and at 138 V, 30 Hz, core loss =500 W
Let, \(V_1=230 V, \;f_1=50Hz\)
\[\begin{aligned} \text{Eddy current loss} &=P_{e1} \\ \text{Hysteresis loss}&=P_{h1} \\ V_2=138V &, f_230Hz \\ \text{Eddy current loss} &=P_{e2} \\ \text{Hysteresis loss}&=P_{h2} \\ \text{we know that, } & \\ \text{Eddy current loss,}\;& P_e \propto B_m^2f^2 \\ \text{and hysteresis loss,}&P_h \propto B_m^xf\propto B_m^1.6 f \\ &(\text{Typical value of x=1.6}) \end{aligned}\]
The transformer induced emf equation is:
\[\begin{aligned} V_1 &=\sqrt{2} \pi \phi _m N \\ V_1&= \sqrt{2} \pi f B_m A N\\ \text{where,}\;\; \frac{V}{t} &=\text{constant} \end{aligned}\]
i.e. flux = constant ( to avoid over fluxing)
\[\begin{aligned} \text{Eddy current loss,} &P_e \propto V^2 \\ \text{and hysteresis loss,}&P_h \propto\frac{V^{1.6}}{f^{0.6}} \end{aligned}\]
\[\begin{aligned} \frac{P_{e2}}{P_{e1}} &=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^2=\left ( \frac{138}{230} \right )^2=0.36 \\ \text{or,} \;\; P_{e2} &= 0.36P_{e1}\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Also,} \;\;\frac{P_{h2}}{P_{e1}} &=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{f_1}{f_2} \right )^{0.6}\\ &=\left ( \frac{138}{230} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{50}{30} \right )^{0.6} \\ &= (0.6)^{1.6} \times \frac{1}{(0.6)^{0.6}}=0.6\\ \therefore \;\; P_{h2} &=0.6P_{h1} \;\;...(ii) \end{aligned}\]
Given at 230V, 50Hz
\(\text{Core loss}=P_{e1}+P_{h1}=1050W\;\;...(iii)\)
At 138V, 30Hz,
\(\text{Core loss}=P_{e2}+P_{h2}=500W\)
or, \(0.36P_{e1}+0.6P_{h1}=500W\;\;...(iv)\)
solving equation (iii) and (iv), we get
\(P_{h1}=508W\) and \(P_{e1}=542W\)
Therefore, hysteresis and eddy current losses at 230V, 50Hz are 508W and 542W respectively.

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question: A 15 kW, 230 V dc shunt motor has armature circuit resistance of 0.4 \(\Omega\) and field circuit resistance of 230 \(\Omega\) . At no load and rated voltage, the motor runs at 1400 rpm and the line current drawn by the motor is 5 A. At full load, the motor draws a line current of 70 A. Neglect armature reaction. The full load speed of the motor in rpm is_____.
questions.explanation:
Given, \(R_a=0.4\Omega ,\) \(R_f=230\Omega ,\) \(V=230 \;\text{volt}\)
At no load, speed, \(N_0=1400 \;\text{rpm},\) \(I_{L_0}=5A\)
Field current, \(I_f=\frac{V}{R_f}=\frac{230}{230}=1A\)

No load armature current, \(I_{a_0}=5-1=4A\)
Induced emf at no-load,
\(E_{a_0}=V-I_{a_0}R_a\)
\(\;\; \;\;=230-4 \times 0.4=228.4 V\)
Also, at full load,
\(I_{L_{fl}}=70A\)
\(I_{a_{fl}}=I_{L_{fl}}-I_f=70-1=69A\)
Induced emf at full load,
\(E_{a_{fl}}=V-I_{a{fl}}R_a\)
\(E_{a_{fl}}=230 -69 \times 0.4=202.4V\)
we know that,
\[\begin{aligned} E_a&\propto \phi \omega _m \alpha \propto N \\ E_a &\propto N \\ (\text{as flux} \; \phi \; &\text{is constant in shunt motor}) \\ \therefore \; \frac{E_{a_{fl}}}{E_{a_{0}}} &=\frac{N_{fl}}{N_0} \\ N_{fl}&= \frac{E_{a_{fl}}}{E_{a_{0}}} \times N_0 \\ &=\left ( \frac{202.4}{228.4} \right ) \times 1400 \end{aligned}\]
Therefore, full-load speed of motor = 1240.63 rpm

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question: A 3 phase, 50 Hz, six pole induction motor has a rotor resistance of 0.1\(\Omega\) and reactance of 0.92\(\Omega\) . Neglect the voltage drop in stator and assume that the rotor resistance is constant. Given that the full load slip is 3%, the ratio of maximum torque to full load torque is
questions.explanation:
Given,
\[\begin{aligned} R'_2 &=0.1\Omega \\ X'_2&= 0.92\Omega \\ S_{fl}&=3\%=0.03 \end{aligned}\]
Slip at maximum torque,
\(S_m=\frac{R'_2}{X'_2}=\frac{0.1}{0.92}=0.1087\)
We know that,
\[\begin{aligned}\frac{T_{fl}}{T_{em}}&=\frac{2}{\left ( \frac{S_m}{S_{fl}}+\frac{S_{fl}}{S_m} \right )}\\ \therefore \;\; \frac{T_{fl}}{T_{em}}&=\frac{2}{\left ( \frac{0.1087}{0.03}+\frac{0.03}{0.1087} \right )}\\ &=\frac{2}{3.623+0.275}=\frac{2}{3.898}\\ \frac{T_{em}}{T_{fl}}&= 1.949 \end{aligned}\]
Therefore, ratio of maximum torque to full-load torque \(=\frac{T_{em}}{T_{fl}}= 1.949\)

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question:
A three phase synchronous generator is to be connected to the infinite bus. The lamps are connected as shown in the figure for the synchronization. The phase sequence of bus voltage is R-Y-B and that of incoming generator voltage is R' - Y' - B'.

It was found that the lamps are becoming dark in the sequence \(L_a-L_b-L_c\). It means that the phase sequence of incoming generator is
options: opposite to infinite bus and its frequency is more than infinite bus
opposite to infinite bus but its frequency is less than infinite bus
same as infinite bus and its frequency is more than infinite bus
same as infinite bus and its frequency is less than infinite bus
questions.explanation:
As,
\[\begin{aligned} L_a \; \text{is connected between R-R'} & \\ L_b \; \text{is connected between Y-Y'} & \\ L_c \; \text{is connected between B-B'} & \\ \end{aligned}\]
therefore, the given method of synchronization is called "synchronization by dark lmap method".
In this method of synchronization, correct phase sequence of the incoming generator is obtain when all the three lamps become dark together and bright together. Since lamps are becoming dark in the sequence \(L_a-L_b-L_c\) therefore, the phase sequence of incoming generator is opposite to the infinite bus.

questions.subject: power-systems
questions.question:
A distribution feeder of 1 km length having resistance, but negligible reactance, is fed from both the ends by 400 V, 50 Hz balanced sources. Both voltage sources \(S_1 \; and \; S_2\) are in phase. The feeder supplies concentrated loads of unity power factor as shown in the figure.
The contributions of \(S_1 \; and \; S_2\) in 100 A current supplied at location P respectively, are
questions.explanation:
Let the resistance of whole length of feeder be \(R\;\Omega\), length of feeder =1000m.
\(\therefore \;\) Resistance per unit length \(=\frac{R}{1000}\Omega /meter\)
\(\therefore \;\) Resistance of 400 m length \(=\frac{R}{1000} \times 400 =\frac{2R}{5} \Omega\)
\(\therefore \;\) Resistance of 200 m length \(=\frac{R}{5} \Omega\)
Let the current supplied by the sources be \(I_1 \text{ and } I_2\).

Applying KVL from source \(S_1 \text{ and } S_2\), we have:
\[\begin{aligned} 400 &= \frac{2R}{5}I_1+\frac{R}{5}(I_1-200)\\ & -\frac{R}{5}(I_2-200)-\frac{R}{5}I_2+400\\ 0&= \frac{2}{5}I_1 +\frac{I_1-200}{5}+\frac{200-I_2}{5}-\frac{I_2}{5}\\ 0&=2I_1+I_1-200+200-I_2-I_2 \\ 0&=3I_1-2I_2\\ I_1&=\frac{2}{3}I_2\;\;\;...(i)\\ \text{also, }& I_1 +I_2-400=100\\ \text{or, }&I_1+I_2=500 \;\;\;...(ii)\\ &\text{Solvinf eq. (i) and (ii), we have}\\ I_1&=200A \text{ and }I_2=300A\\ &\text{Contribution of }S_1 \text{in 100 A at location}\\ P&=I_1-200=0A \\ &\text{Contribution of }S_2 \text{in 100 A at location}\\ P&=I_2-200=300-200=100A \end{aligned}\]
Therefore, \(S_2\) alone supplies the total load at location P.

questions.subject: power-systems
questions.question:
A two bus power system shown in the figure supplies load of 1.0+j0.5 p.u.

The values of \(V_1\) in p.u. and \(\delta _2\) respectively are
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} P_2+jQ_2&=(1.0+j0.5)p.u.\\ P_2&=1=\frac{|V_1||V_2|}{|X|} \sin (\delta _1-\delta _2)\\ 1&=\frac{V_1}{0.1}\sin (-\delta _2)\\ -\frac{0.1}{\sin (-\delta _2)}&=V_1\;\;...(i)\\ Q_2&=0.5=\frac{|V_2|}{|X|}(|V_1| \cos \delta _2 -|V_2|)\\ 0.5&=\frac{1}{0.1}(V_1 \cos \delta _2-1)\\ \frac{1.05}{\cos \delta _2}&=V_1\;\;...(ii)\\ &\text{From equation (i) and (ii),}\\ \tan \delta _2&=\frac{-0.1}{1.05}\\ \delta _2&=-5.44^{\circ}\\ \text{substituting } & \delta _2 \text{ value in equation (ii) gives,}\\ V_1&=1.05\;p.u. \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: power-systems
questions.question:
The fuel cost functions of two power plants are

Plant \(P_1:C_1\equiv 0.05Pg^2_1+APg_1+B\)
Plant \(P_2:C_2\equiv 0.10Pg^2_2+3APg_2+2B\)

where, \(Pg_1 \; and \; Pg_2\) are the generated powers of two plants, and A and B are the constants. If the two plants optimally share 1000 MW load at incremental fuel cost of 100 Rs/MWh, the ratio of load shared by plants \(P_1 \; and \; P_2\) is
questions.explanation:
Given, \(P_{g1}+P_{g2}=1000 \;\;...(i)\)
Also, incremental cost of production of
\(g_1=\frac{dC_1}{dP_{g1}}=0.1P_{g1}+A \;\;\;...(ii)\)
and incremental cost of production of
\(g_2=\frac{dC_2}{dP_{g2}}=0.2P_{g2}+3A\;\;\;...(iii)\)
For optimum load sharing
\[\begin{aligned} \frac{dC_1}{dP_{g1}}&=\frac{dC_2}{dP_{g2}} \\ 0.1P_{g1}+A&=0.2P_{g2}+3A \\ 0.1P_{g1}-0.2P_{g2}&=2A \\ P_{g1}-2P_{g2}&=20A \;\;\;...(iv) \\ \text{Given, } \frac{dC_1}{dP_{g1}}&=\frac{dC_2}{dP_{g2}}=100\; Rs/MWh \end{aligned}\]
Putting this value in equation (ii), we have
\[\begin{aligned} 100&=0.1P_{g1}+A\\ A&=(100-0.1P_{g1})\;\;...(v) \end{aligned}\]
Using equation (iv) and (v), we have:
\[\begin{aligned} P_{g1}-2P_{g2}&=20(100-0.1P_{g1})\\ 3P_{g1}-2P_{g2}&=20004\;\;...(vi) \end{aligned}\] \[\begin{aligned} P_{g1}&=800MW \text{ and } P_{g2}=200MW\\ \therefore \;P_{g1}:P_{g2}&=800:200=4:1 \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: power-systems
questions.question:
The over current relays for the line protection and loads connected at the buses are shown in the figure.

The relays are IDMT in nature having the characteristic

\(t_{op}=\frac{0.14\times Time \; Multipller \; Setting}{(Plug \; Setting \; Multiplier)^{0.02}-1}\)

The maximum and minimum fault currents at bus B are 2000 A and 500 A respectively. Assuming the time multiplier setting and plug setting for relay \(R_B\) to be 0.1 and 5 A respectively, the operating time of \(R_B\) (in seconds) is_____.
questions.explanation:
Minimum and maximum fault currents are
\(I_{fmin}=500A, I_{fmax}=2000A\)
For relay \(R_B,\;TMS=0.1\), plug setting =5A
\[\begin{aligned} \text{PSM}&=\frac{I_f}{I_{pk} \times \text{C.T. ratio}} \\ \text{C.T. ratio} &=\frac{\text{Full load current}}{I_{pk}} \\ &= \frac{100}{5}\\ \text{At realy, }&R_B\\ \text{with }I_{fmin}\Rightarrow & \text{PSM}_1=\frac{500}{\frac{100}{5}\times 5}=5\\ \text{with }I_{fmax}\Rightarrow & \text{PSM}_2=\frac{2000}{\frac{100}{5}\times 5}=20 \end{aligned}\]
Operating time with TMS=0.1,
and from IDMT characterisrics
\(t_{op_2}=\frac{0.14 \times 0.1}{(20)^{0.02}-1}=0.226sec\)

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: For the given system, it is desired that the system be stable. The minimum value of \(\alpha\) for this condition is ______.
questions.explanation:
Given, \(G(s)=\frac{(s+\alpha )}{s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+(\alpha -1)s+(1-\alpha )}\)
and \(H(s)=1\)
Characteristic equation of given control system is given by
\(1+G(s)H(s)=0\)
or, \(1+\left [ \frac{s+\alpha }{s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+(\alpha -1)s+(1-\alpha )} \right ]=0\)
or, \(s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+(\alpha -1)s+(1-\alpha )+s+\alpha =0\)
or, \(s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+\alpha s+1=0\)
Routh's array is

For the given system to be stable, there should not be any sign change in the first column of Routh's array.
Therefore, \(1+\alpha \gt 0 \;or, \; \alpha \gt -1\;\; ...(i)\)
Also, \(\frac{\alpha ^2 +\alpha -1}{1+\alpha } \gt 0\)
or, \(\alpha ^2 +\alpha -1 \gt 0\)
or, \((\alpha +1.618)(\alpha -0.618) \gt 0\)
or, \(\alpha \lt -1.618\)
or, \(\alpha \gt 0.618\)
As \(\alpha \gt -1\) (using equation (i))
therefore, \(\alpha \gt 0.618 \;\;...(ii)\)
Combining condition (i) and (ii),
\(-1 \lt \alpha \lt 0.618\)
Thus, for the system to be stable minimum value of \(\alpha =0.618.\)

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question:
The Bode magnitude plot of the transfer function \(G(s)=\frac{K(1+0.5s)(1+as)}{s(1+\frac{s}{8})(1+bs)(1+\frac{s}{36})}\) is shown below:
Note that -6 dB/octave =- 20 dB/decade. The value of \(\frac{a}{bK}\) is _____.
questions.explanation:
Given, \(G(s)=\frac{K(1+0.5s)(1+as)}{s(1+\frac{s}{8})(1+bs)(1+\frac{s}{36})}\)
(1+as) is addition of zero to the transfer function whose contribution in slope=+20 dB/decade or -6 dB/octave.
(1+bs) is addition of pole to the transfer function whose contribution in slope=-20 dB/decade or -6 dB/octave.
Observing the change in the slope at different corner frequencies, we conclude that,
\(a=\frac{1}{4}\) rad/s and \(b=\frac{1}{24}\) rad/s
From\(\omega =0.01\) rad/s to \(\omega =8\) rad/s,
slope=-20dB/decade
Let the vertical length in dB by y
\(\therefore \;\; -20=\left ( \frac{0-y}{log8-log0.01} \right )\)
\(\;\;\;\; -20=\frac{y}{log 8+2}\)
\(\;\;\;\; y=58 dB\)
Applying, \(y-mx+C\) at \(\omega =0.01\) rad/s,
We have, \(58=-20log 0.01 +C\)
\(C=58-40=18\)
Now, \(C=20logK\)
\(LogK=\frac{18}{20}=0.9\)
\(\therefore \;\; K= log^{-1}(0.9)=(10)^{0.9}=7.94\)
\(\therefore \;\; \frac{a}{bK}=\frac{\left ( \frac{1}{4} \right )}{\left ( \frac{1}{24} \right )\times 7.94}=\frac{24}{4 \times 7.94}=0.755\)

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question:
A system matrix is given as follows
\[A=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & -1\\ -6& -11&6 \\ -6 & -11 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\]
The absolute value of the ratio of the maximum eigenvalue to the minimum eigenvalue is _______.
questions.explanation:
Characteristic equation \(|A-\lambda I|=0\)
\[\begin{aligned} \begin{vmatrix} -\lambda & 1 & -1\\ -6 & -11-\lambda & 6\\ -6&-11 & 5-\lambda \end{vmatrix} = 0\\ \Rightarrow \; -\lambda [-55+11\lambda -5\lambda +\lambda ^2+66] \\ -1[-30+6\lambda +36]-1[66-66-6\lambda ]=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; -\lambda (\lambda ^2+6\lambda +11)-1(6\lambda +6)+6\lambda =0 \\ \Rightarrow \;-\lambda ^3-6\lambda ^2-11\lambda -6=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\lambda ^3+6\lambda ^2+11\lambda +6=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; (\lambda +1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda +3)=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\lambda =-1,-2,-3 \end{aligned}\]
The absolute values of \(\lambda\) are \(|\lambda |=1,2,3\)
Ratio of maximum and minimum eigen value is \(=3:1=\frac{3}{1}=3\)

questions.subject: electrical-electronic-measurements
questions.question:
The dc current flowing in a circuit is measured by two ammeters, one PMMC
and another electrodynamometer type, connected in series. The PMMC meter
contains 100 turns in the coil, the flux density in the air gap is 0.2Wb/\(m^2\), and
the area of the coil is 80 \(mm^2\). The electrodynamometer ammeter has a change in
mutual inductance with respect to deflection of 0.5 mH/deg. The spring constants
of both the meters are equal. The value of current, at which the deflections of the
two meters are same, is ______
questions.explanation:
For a PMMC ammeter, at equilibrim, we have :
controlling torque (\(T_c\))=Deflecting torque(\(T_d\))
\[\begin{aligned} K\theta _1 &=GI \; \text{or}\; \theta _1=\frac{GI}{K}\\ where, \;\; G &= nBA\\ \therefore \; \theta _1 &= \frac{nBAI}{K} \end{aligned}\]
For an electrodynometer ammeter, at equilibrium,
Controlling torque=Deflecting torque
\[\begin{aligned} i.e. \;\; T_c &=T_d \; \text{or}\; K \theta _2=I^2 \frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; \theta _2 &= \frac{I^2}{K}\cdot \frac{dM}{d\theta }\;\;...(ii)\\ \end{aligned}\]

For the deflection in the two meter to be same,
\[\begin{aligned} \theta _1 &=\theta _2\\ or, \;\; \frac{nBAI}{K} &= \frac{I^2}{K}\cdot \frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; nBA&=I\frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; I &=\frac{nBA}{\left ( \frac{dM}{d\theta } \right )} \end{aligned}\]
\[\begin{aligned} Given, \;\; n&= \text{number of turns}=100\\ B&= 0.2 Wb/m^2\\ A&=80mm^2=80 \times 10^{-6}m^2\\ \text{and}\;\; \frac{dM}{d\theta }&=0.5 mH/rad\\ &=0.5 \times 10^{-3}H/rad \\ \end{aligned}\]
Putting the values in I, we get
\[\begin{aligned} I &=\left ( \frac{100 \times 0.2 \times 80 \times 10^{-6}}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} \right ) A\\ &= \frac{1.6}{0.5}=3.2A \end{aligned}\]
\(\therefore\) Required value of current,
\(I=3.2Amp.\)

questions.subject: power-electronics
questions.question: The figure shows one period of the output voltage of an inverter. \(\alpha\) should be chosen such that \(60^{\circ} \lt \alpha \lt 90^{\circ}\). If rms value of the fundamental component is 50V, then \(\alpha\) in degree is _____.
questions.explanation:
The output voltage \(V_0\) can be reprresnted by fourier series as under:
\[\begin{aligned} V_0&=\sum_{n=1,3,5,...}^{\infty }a_n \cos n\omega t+b_n \sin n\omega t\\ \text{where, } a_n&=\frac{2}{T}\int_{0}^{T}f(t)\cos n\omega t \;d(\omega t) \\ b_n&=\frac{2}{T}\int_{0}^{T}f(t)\sin n\omega t \;d(\omega t) \\ a_n&=\frac{1}{\pi} [\int_{0}^{\alpha }100 \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{\alpha }^{180^{\circ}-\alpha }(-100) \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t) \\ &+ \int_{180^{\circ}-\alpha}^{180^{\circ} }100 \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{180^{\circ} }^{180^{\circ}+\alpha }(-100) \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t)\\ &+ \int_{180^{\circ}+\alpha}^{360^{\circ} -\alpha }100 \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{360^{\circ}-\alpha }^{360^{\circ} }(-100) \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t)]\\ a_n &=\frac{100}{\pi}[\sin \alpha - \sin (180^{\circ} -\alpha ) + \sin \alpha \\ &+\sin (180^{\circ}) -\sin (180^{\circ} -\alpha )\\ &- \sin (180^{\circ} +\alpha ) + \sin 180^{\circ}\\ &+ \sin (360^{\circ} -\alpha )- \sin (180^{\circ} +\alpha ) \\ &- \sin (360^{\circ} ) + \sin (360^{\circ} -\alpha )]\\ a_n &=0 \\ b_n&=\frac{1}{\pi} [\int_{0}^{\alpha }100 \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{\alpha }^{180^{\circ}-\alpha }(-100) \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t) \\ &+ \int_{180^{\circ}-\alpha}^{180^{\circ} }100 \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{180^{\circ} }^{180^{\circ}+\alpha }(-100) \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t)\\ &+ \int_{180^{\circ}+\alpha}^{360^{\circ} -\alpha }100 \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{360^{\circ}-\alpha }^{360^{\circ} }(-100) \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t)]\\ b_n &=\frac{100}{\pi}[-\cos \alpha +1+ \cos (180^{\circ} -\alpha ) - \cos \alpha \\ &-\cos (180^{\circ}) +\cos (180^{\circ} -\alpha )\\ &+ \cos (180^{\circ} +\alpha ) - \cos 180^{\circ}\\ &- \cos (360^{\circ} -\alpha )+ \cos (180^{\circ} +\alpha ) \\ &+ \cos (360^{\circ} ) - \cos (360^{\circ} -\alpha )]\\ b_n&=\frac{100}{\pi}[4-8 \cos \alpha ] =50\sqrt{2}\\ \cos \alpha &=0.22231=77.15^{\circ} \end{aligned}\]
